object_owner.description: Owns every object. A NOLOGIN role no service connects as; migrations SET LOCAL ROLE into it and RESET before dbmate stamps the version.

app_runtime.description: The runtime identity permitted on app.* directly. Still policy-bound: the tables carry FORCE row-level security.

anon.description: The role an unauthenticated request becomes. Granted schema USAGE and nothing else.

authenticated.description: A request carrying a validated identity from Session 6 onward. Reads through api views, writes through the RPCs.

agent_writer.description: Agent identity permitted to call the write RPCs.

api_documentation.description: The role the OpenAPI capture and the documentation page read the published surface as. Holds view SELECT and EXECUTE on the write RPCs, which is what makes openapi-mode = follow-privileges publish the whole surface; the pre-request hook refuses it a request identity, so it can never perform what it advertises. Outputs schema v6, D158.

api_documentation_name.description: The same role, as a string literal rather than a quoted identifier, for the hook's `current_user::text = ...` comparison. Two placeholders over ONE source: they resolve from the same key in the same document, so they cannot name different roles -- which a second source, or a name written out beside the grant, could.

auth_service.description: The auth service's database identity. Session 6. Migration 0011 grants it schema USAGE and nothing else -- its LOGIN attribute, connection limit, SCRAM credential and statement_timeout are bootstrap-plane work, because anything ALTER ROLE is (D102), and the functions it will call arrive with the code that calls them.

project_admin.description: The administrator's request role, and a request role only from Session 6 Run 9: before that it existed, NOLOGIN and unreachable, because the authenticator held no membership in it. What it may do ADMINISTRATIVELY is not decided here or by the role name -- it is decided by the scope in the token, which is what API-ADMIN-001 states and why a project_admin without admin_users:write is refused. The membership is granted by the bootstrap plane (D266, D102); this placeholder exists so migration 0013 can give the role schema USAGE and the EXECUTE every request role needs to run the pre-request hook.

storage_service.description: The storage runtime's database identity. Session 7. The role has been in naming.ROLE_SUFFIXES since Session 3 as a NOLOGIN stub with a null verifier, so 0014 creates nothing and activates nothing (D307): its LOGIN attribute, connection limit, SCRAM credential and statement_timeout are bootstrap-plane work, because anything ALTER ROLE is (D102). This file grants it EXECUTE on seven SECURITY DEFINER functions and no privilege of any kind on app_private.storage_objects -- which is what makes 'the service cannot read another owner's row even by composing its own SQL' a property of the catalog rather than of the service's code.

migrations.name: schemas_and_default_privileges
migrations.description: The four schemas, pgvector in extensions rather than public, and a default-deny posture for function execution.

migrations.name: project_identity_and_ledger
migrations.description: The single-row identity sentinel that binds this volume to one project, and the ledger recording which bytes each version applied.

migrations.name: owner_scoped_tables_and_forced_rls
migrations.description: notes and tasks under FORCE row-level security, keyed on a transaction-local identity claim that denies when absent.

migrations.name: security_invoker_api_views
migrations.description: Read-only api views that run with the caller's authority, so the underlying row policy still applies.

migrations.name: write_rpcs
migrations.description: Two write functions that derive ownership from the request identity and take no owner parameter.

migrations.name: app_runtime_least_privilege
migrations.description: The application runtime role loses the direct reach into app and app_private that Session 3 granted it, default privileges included, and holds only what membership in authenticated carries. See SEC-DBX-002 and ADR 0041.

migrations.name: api_surface_convergence
migrations.description: ADR 0048: the catalog converges on the domain four documents froze. notes.body becomes content, tasks gains description and a bounded api.task_status derived from done, create_task is retired for update_task_status, and the api views and write RPCs are rebuilt over the result.

migrations.name: http_request_plane
migrations.description: app_private.postgrest_pre_request(), and the one private object an HTTP request role may reach: USAGE on app_private plus EXECUTE on that function, granted by name to anon and authenticated and to nothing else. See ADR 0052 and D138.

migrations.name: documentation_role
migrations.description: The documentation role's grants -- view SELECT plus EXECUTE on both write RPCs, which is what makes openapi-mode = follow-privileges publish the whole surface -- and the pre-request clause that refuses it a request identity, so the RPCs it advertises are ones it can never perform. See D158.

migrations.name: request_statement_timeout
migrations.description: The pre-request hook carries the request role's statement_timeout into the request transaction. PostgreSQL processes a role's settings only at login, and PostgREST reaches its request role with SET LOCAL ROLE -- so the timeouts ADR 0067 put on the roles bounded nothing. The value is still the document's; this reads what the bootstrap plane wrote and applies it for one transaction. See D198, ADR 0068.

migrations.name: identity_registry
migrations.description: The identity registry: app_private.users, user_credentials, agents, agent_credentials and auth_contract_state, plus the is_scope_set helper the scope columns are checked against. Created from nothing -- the runbook's 'extend the existing users table' has no subject, so every column is NOT NULL from creation and the backfill is struck rather than written over zero rows (D218). No foreign key reaches app.notes.owner_id: that column holds a claim value and ADR 0029 states in its title that it is trusted, not authenticated. auth_service is granted schema USAGE and nothing else; the functions it will call arrive with the code that calls them. See ADR 0078, D218, D228.

migrations.name: auth_access_plane
migrations.description: The access plane for human subjects: eight SECURITY DEFINER functions in app_private, granted to auth_service, which are the only way the service reaches the identity registry -- 0011 granted it schema USAGE and nothing else and said these would arrive with the code that calls them. Lookup is by the same normalised expression the unique index uses, and returns no row rather than raising for an unknown username, because the login path exists to make 'no such user' and 'wrong password' indistinguishable. auth_bootstrap_administrator takes a project-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock derived from project_identity: measured, two concurrent callers without it both read 'no administrator' and both insert. It is NOT granted to auth_service -- a service that could call it is the public bootstrap endpoint that does not exist. The blanket REVOKE FROM PUBLIC is load-bearing rather than tidy: a new function is PUBLIC-executable by default and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES records nothing for functions (D262). This is 0012 and Run 9's hook becomes 0013 (D261). See ADR 0084, D261, D262.

migrations.name: agent_plane_and_current_state_hook
migrations.description: The pre-request hook stops trusting a signature, and agents get the access plane 0012 gave humans. Until now the hook read `sub` and took the rest of the token on the strength of a valid signature; from here credential_version, authz_version, role and sorted scope are compared against current state inside the request's own transaction and any mismatch is refused -- which is what makes a disable, a password reset or a scope change take effect on the next request rather than at the next expiry (SEC-REV-001). The comparison goes through a SECURITY DEFINER helper returning a BOOLEAN over the whole claim tuple, never the subject's own values: a function answering 'what are X's scopes' would let any authenticated caller enumerate authority through a hook it cannot avoid running. project_admin becomes a request role and gets USAGE and EXECUTE; its authenticator MEMBERSHIP is the bootstrap plane's, not this file's (D266, D102). The agent roles stay ungranted, so an agent token fails at role switching before the hook runs. This is 0013 and the plan called it 0012 (D261). See D261, D266, D267.

migrations.name: object_storage_plane
migrations.description: The object-storage plane: app_private.storage_objects under a one-way pending -> available -> tombstoned state machine, storage_contract_state, and seven SECURITY DEFINER functions granted to storage_service and to nothing else. The service holds no privilege of any kind on the table, so a defect in it cannot read another owner's row even by composing its own SQL, and the proof attempts the read rather than asking has_table_privilege (D103). The download lookup answers absent, foreign, pending and tombstoned identically -- a caller that could tell them apart could enumerate another user's ids (STO-OWN-001), and that filter is the linearization point a committed tombstone precedes. Completion is a compare-and-set on state = pending, so it is idempotent and returns the current state rather than raising. The cleanup claim carries both halves of ADR 0104: the lease predicate is the correctness mechanism, because the provider DELETE happens outside the transaction and a row lock is released at COMMIT and at crash, and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is throughput only -- both measured on the locked pg18 digest with controls. Every CHECK was written against ADR 0080: a CHECK passes when its expression is NULL, so the coherence constraints are shaped to be total while the column checks are deliberately partial where the column is nullable. Does not touch the pre-request hook (D270). This is 0014 and the runbook called it 0012 (D312). See ADR 0104, D57, D262, D285, D307.

migrations.name: storage_completion_key
migrations.description: app_private.storage_completion_key(uuid, uuid) -- the one function 0014 needed and did not have. Completion must ask the provider how many bytes arrived before it moves an object to available, and to ask it needs the object's key; 0014 exposed the key only through storage_lookup_for_download (state = available) and storage_claim_cleanup_batch (state = tombstoned), so the pending state completion operates on was the one state with no reader. The alternative -- returning the key from storage_create_upload_intent and having the client hand it back -- is refused by STO-KEY-001, whose whole content is that no client-supplied key can reach a presign. This is 0015 and not an edit to 0014 because ADR 0091's three conditions were checked rather than assumed: no cluster holds 0014, but 0014 APPLIES perfectly well, and the ADR says in as many words that a migration which merely did the wrong thing does not qualify for in-place correction. The state predicate is pending OR available, not pending alone: the pending-only version broke idempotency (STO-COMPLETE-001), because a retried completion 404s before reaching the compare-and-set that makes it idempotent -- 0014's own comment calls that CAS idempotent, which was true of the function and false of the path through it. Tombstoned stays excluded, since completing one would resurrect it and the state machine is one-way. Owner and state are one predicate, so absent, foreign and tombstoned return zero rows alike (STO-OWN-001). EXECUTE to storage_service only, with an explicit REVOKE FROM PUBLIC beside the CREATE because a new function is PUBLIC-executable and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES records nothing for functions (D57, re-measured as D262). Relies on the schema USAGE 0014 granted and does not re-grant it (D337). See ADR 0091, ADR 0104, D348.
